holidays.name: National Cheesecake Day
holidays.description: A day for treating yourself to a slice of creamy, dreamy cheesecake. Plain, strawberry-topped, or swirled with cookie dough, every version counts. Many bakeries and restaurants mark the day with specials and discounts.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance that has been celebrated on July 30 for years. Its exact founder is unclear. It has become a regular fixture on the dessert calendar.
holidays.funFact: Cheesecake is one of the oldest desserts around. Food historians trace early versions to ancient Greece, where cheese cakes were served to athletes at the early Olympic Games.

holidays.name: Father-in-Law Day
holidays.description: A day to recognize the often-underappreciated dad of your spouse. Send a card, share a meal, or just say thanks for raising the person you love.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance in the United States that falls on July 30. It gives in-laws their own moment after Father's Day. Its precise origin is unclear.
holidays.funFact: Father-in-Law Day sits in the calendar right next to National Cheesecake Day. That makes a slice of cake an easy gift.

holidays.name: World Snorkeling Day
holidays.description: A salute to splashing around face-down in the shallows, watching fish go about their day. All you need is a mask, a snorkel, and some curiosity about what's under the waves.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It celebrates one of the easiest ways to explore the underwater world.
holidays.funFact: Ancient divers are said to have breathed through hollow reeds while underwater. That makes the snorkel one of the oldest pieces of diving gear.
